precedence_rules.rule: Errata override the baseline at the cited spec lines; the spec file stays byte-identical; E-5 is a clarification, the rest corrections; errata Sec. B lists companion claims needing no change.
Baseline conventions C1-C13 govern every document unless an erratum says otherwise (only E-8 touches Sec. 0, C12).

Addendum C14-C17 and Secs. 11-19 extend and never override; where the errata names an addendum line, read the errata over it; elsewhere the addendum is the document of record for grammar coverage, capacity, hybrid, discourse/MPS, positioning, memory table, export extension C15.

Review verdicts govern over the companion's wording; 'Correct' in RV rows corrects the third-party discussion, never the baseline; companion adoption conditional on review conditions (i)-(v), only (i) discharged.

Companion requirements are constraints binding only when mapped to a document of record or recorded as gaps; its technical corrections are superseded by the errata; requirements of companion Secs. 10-12.8 and 14 are deferred until P0 reports.

Hardware-limits report is advisory; cites the addendum where they overlap; its labels and LIM-* conventions apply only inside kernels imported from it (LIM-n are inventory ids absent from the limits file; resolve by the limits line quoted beside them, bridge Sec. 3.1, e.g. LIM-12 = limits Sec. 2.2 (8)(iii) l473-474); its 'replaces' statements are scoped to the objectives it introduces; its Haar-expectation figures never replace exact conventions.

UNVERIFIED beats asserted: only CONFIRMED errata, normative spec/addendum text, or a listed fp64 program establish a statement; nothing in the set is measured on a device; register residency is a ptxas target.

Numeric precedence per claim: verify_c (Sec. 8 numbers) > errata > review > addendum > limits > spec > companion; recompute downstream numbers by the governing formula and label UNVERIFIED; rounding differences are not conflicts; review self-corrections resolve to the later value.
Unresolved conflict: record it (topic, a, b, resolution, rule), prefer the more recent derivation backed by a program, flag to the engineer with proposed erratum text; never resolve silently in code.

Symbol namespacing: spec C9/Sec. 0 symbols keep their meaning; other uses qualified (D_V, D_s, depth D, S_q15, S(rho), N_nouns, m_arg); canonical d_n, d_s; ids Cn, Tn, (S.n), (11.n)-(19.n) reserved; other documents' same-shaped ids cited with a prefix.

Form scoping: circuit-form rules (C11, sign_k = -1, shift rules, W_hw) apply to the bent-wire circuit; tree-form rules (11.7, sign_k = +1, C16) to Sec. 11 sentences on the simulator; C17 to DisCoCirc registers; LIM-7/8/NU.5 to density-matrix kernels; every gate carries its form.
Exact conventions (C8 Bell factor, (1.4) P_post, D = Z) are never replaced by Haar expectations (E[Z], E[P_post], A = 2^{q_n}); expectations serve floors, p_min, format selection only.
KB = 1024 B; exact byte figures govern over shorthand ('100 KB' = 100,000 B); documents identified by SHA-256, not path.

Registered companions (1.2): puremath is authoritative for proofs and statements of results and ranks with the review for derivations, below the errata for any spec line; engineering documents (spec with errata, addendum, limits for its own themes, verify.c for what it prints) remain authoritative for implementation values; a puremath number is still ranked by R8, disagreements go to R9, baseline changes need an erratum; puremath Appendix B items carry no authority. dsdm is authoritative for schedule, priority (MoSCoW) and acceptance sequencing only, has no technical precedence and inherits R1-R13.
